description: A project you mark for auto-delegate lets a session's agent call the delegate tool before a heavy command. When this computer has no room, Carnivore copies the working folder into a side repository, the other computer runs the command in its own job folder, and the changed files are applied back here. The mark is off by default and an agent's delegate waits for your approval unless Beast Mode is on. A job can also be a task: delegate takes a task and an optional agent type, the other computer starts a normal visible session of the same harness (claude or codex) in the job folder, and its changed files, closing text and token usage come back. A worker's question parks the job for job_reply, and the caller is told once when a job needs it. The worker runs under a login the other computer chooses, never your credentials, and git push is blocked by default (not a sandbox). A job can also say what it needs (tools, a GPU, memory, an owner label): a job no computer can run is refused with a plain reason, a missing tool on the other computer can be installed with Homebrew after you approve, copies stay in sync and warmed ahead of the first job, and a counter shows how much heavy work stayed home. The jobs have a screen, the Pack page's jobs tab, with the numbers on work that stayed home, and a count on the session row.
examples: Run the whole test suite on the idle computer while this one keeps its CPU for you.
Build a project on a computer that already has its dependencies installed and get the build output back.
Stop a runaway job from its agent with job_stop and have the other computer free its folder.
Ask a worker on the idle computer to write the missing tests for a module and get the new files back with what it said and what it cost.
See that the studio computer has the ios simulator and is not pegged before you send it a build.
Label a computer rtx 4090, then let an agent ask for it by that label.
See which computer is running the long test run an agent handed off, and stop it from the jobs tab.
Turn auto-delegate off, then press trash on the studio computer's leftover copy and see it go to that computer's trash, while the copy with unfinished work is kept and named.
Spot the 2 jobs badge on a session row and click it to see what that session handed to other computers.
Start a session for a marked project while a test run pegs this computer: auto starts it on the idle computer, in its copy at your last commit.
Pick auto for a project that needs xcode: the session starts on the computer that has it, or the picker says why nobody can.
Send a render to a Windows computer with a big graphics card that runs no carnivore, reached over ssh on port 2222: the card says it runs there over ssh, and the result files come back here.
See that a computer over ssh did not answer, with its last figures shown by age, before an agent sends it a job.
See in the heavy work block that most of this week's test runs ran on the studio computer, and how many hours stayed here while this computer was busy.
Place a job from one member to another with the alpha stopped.
how_to: Right click the project's heading, pick project settings, untick any computer that must never get a copy, then turn on auto-delegate; it copies the project at once.

Turning it off asks nothing: flip the switch in the project settings and it is off. The master stays here and the copies stay on their computers, idle and not syncing. Each copy auto-delegate made is listed as computer: copy kept at folder with a trash button; trash moves it to that computer's trash after its own checks, and a copy with uncommitted work, a stash, commits the master lacks, or a live session is kept with the reason. Copies you made yourself are never listed.
Ask an agent to run a heavy command. It calls delegate first; the answer is either decision here (run it yourself) or a job on another computer.
Approve the card in the approvals inbox. With Beast Mode off the card says Beast Mode would have approved it.
A job that takes longer than one call: the agent calls job_wait with the job id.
If a changed file clashed with an edit you made meanwhile, nothing is applied and the job's version waits on a ref for 24 hours.

Hand over a task instead of a command: the agent calls delegate with task (and agent_type for a named agent). The card shows the task, the worker's permission mode (bypass is a warning line) and the account note. A worker's question comes back as a question answer; answer it with job_reply.
Open the Pack page, pick a computer and read the what it has block: system, chip, memory, gpus, tools and whether it is pegged. Press check again to re-read it now (at most once a minute).
Add or remove a label in the same block; each change saves the whole list at once.
A computer that shows update carnivore on this computer to see what it has runs an older version.
Add needs and prefer to a delegate call, for example needs ["xcode"]; a refused answer names the computers and what each lacks.

Open the Pack page and pick the jobs tab. Live jobs show first with a state tag, the task or command, the computer and project, and how long they have run; the live and all filter adds the older ones, and details shows the exit code, output and result.
Press stop on a live job and confirm; the row changes to stopped when the computer answers. Press open worker on an agent job to open the worker's session.
A session that started live jobs shows a job count on its row; click it to open the jobs tab narrowed to that session, and clear the chip to see every job.
Jobs other computers sent to this one are listed under running here for another computer; they are read only.

Open the launch picker on a marked project, pick auto in the computer row and start: Carnivore says where it started, how many uncommitted files stayed on this computer, and that the work lives on that computer until it pushes or you move it back.
Agents can ask for it: session_create or agent_spawn with placement auto (and needs); the approval card names the computer, the account and the permission mode.
For a blueprint automation, set its computer row to auto: each member without a computer of its own is placed the same way; a member with an opening prompt starts here.

Add the computer in the hosts list, then turn takes-work on for it with its fingerprint: the first try shows the host key to compare, the second (with that fingerprint) pins it. A computer over ssh runs command jobs only, never an agent task, and nothing is installed on it.

Open a project's settings, find what its jobs need under the auto-delegate switch, and type the words a kind of job must have or should prefer; save sends only the kinds you changed, and back to default restores the built-in words.
Open a computer in the Pack page, then its allow lists: pick every project, or only the projects and companies you tick, so a computer never takes work from a project you did not allow.
Remove the copies an ssh computer holds from its block in the computers tab (it asks once).
Jobs go straight from the computer that places them to the member that runs them, over their direct link, and a computer with may host agents off is not offered jobs.
media_exempt: captured at the next version bump; recaptured after the next version bump
name: Auto-delegate
summary: an agent can hand a heavy command, such as a test run or a build, or a whole task for a worker session, to another computer of your pack, and the changed files come back unless one of them clashes with your own edit.
where: a project heading's menu (drawer or sessions page) > project settings > sharing this project between computers

Agent tools delegate, job_reply, job_wait and job_stop, and the owner routes under /pack/jobs and /projects/{name}/auto-delegate. The approval card appears in the approvals inbox. The delegated usage shows in the terminal foot bar. The jobs have a screen: Pack page > jobs.
project settings > auto-delegate > turn the switch off: no dialog; each copy it made is listed with a trash button
Pack page > computers > a computer > overview > what it has (facts, labels, pegged line, check again)
Pack page > jobs (live jobs, history, and the jobs other computers sent here); a session row's job count in the sidebar and on the sessions page
Launch picker > computer (this computer or auto), for a project marked auto-delegate; and a saved blueprint automation's editor > computer row (this computer or auto)
Settings of a computer reached by plain ssh: the hosts list in the app, then the owner routes under /pack/ssh-targets (the agent tool ssh_targets_list only reads them)
project settings > auto-delegate > what its jobs need (per kind: needs, prefer, back to default); Pack page > computers > a computer > allow lists (every project or only the ticked ones)
